name: Penfolds Shiraz St. Henri 2010
text:
## Penfolds Shiraz St. Henri 2010

**The story.** St Henri is older than Penfolds' ownership of it. It began in the 19th century at Auldana, a vineyard and winery next door to Penfolds' [Magill Estate](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Penfolds+Magill+Estate,+Magill,+South+Australia,+Australia&t=k) in the Adelaide foothills, as Auldana's St Henri claret. Penfolds bought Auldana in 1944 ([Wine Spectator](https://www.winespectator.com/articles/penfolds-st-henri-shiraz-old-school-15540)). [Penfolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penfolds) itself goes back to 1844, when an English doctor, [Christopher Rawson Penfold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penfolds), and his wife Mary planted vines at [Magill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magill,_South_Australia) to make fortified wine tonics for his patients; after his death, Mary ran and blended the wines herself ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penfolds)).

In the 1950s, while [Max Schubert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Schubert) was creating [Grange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penfolds_Grange), partly by bringing French oak barrels to Australian dry red wine, his Penfolds colleague John Davoren revived the old Auldana style. Penfolds says his aim was "a genuine claret style" to compare with the greatest wines of [Bordeaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bordeaux_wine), and that the two wines began life together "in a climate of intense excitement, experimentation and research". The first trials were Cabernet Sauvignon and [Mataro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mourv%C3%A8dre), later Shiraz; the first vintages were reportedly foot-stomped in open hogsheads, with plenty of stalks. The first commercial vintage was 1957 ([Penfolds](https://www.penfolds.com/en-au/about-penfolds/news/penfolds-2010-st-henri-a-stand-out-from-impressive-vintage.html)).

**The wine.** St Henri is Grange's opposite. Grange ages in American oak barrels, but St Henri sees no new oak at all: it matures for 12 to 18 months in large old vats, 1,460 litres and more than 50 years old, which add texture but almost no wood flavour. It is mostly [Shiraz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah), sometimes with a little [Cabernet Sauvignon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabernet_Sauvignon), blended from several South Australian regions ([Penfolds](https://www.penfolds.com/en-au/about-penfolds/news/penfolds-2010-st-henri-a-stand-out-from-impressive-vintage.html)). Penfolds calls it "a sentimental favourite amongst collectors", and Wine Spectator calls it "the odd duck" of the Penfolds high-end range: the "sneaky little secret" Australian collectors know is that St Henri can age as long as Grange, for a fraction of the price ([Wine Spectator](https://www.winespectator.com/articles/penfolds-st-henri-shiraz-old-school-15540)).

The 2010 is 100% Shiraz, mainly from the [Barossa Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barossa_Valley_wine_region) and [McLaren Vale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale), "propelled by skin and seed tannins alone" and matured for 18 months in old 1,460-litre oak vats ([Penfolds](https://www.penfolds.com/en-au/about-penfolds/news/penfolds-2010-st-henri-a-stand-out-from-impressive-vintage.html)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [South Australia vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/south-australia) calls 2010 "the year that the rain finally came", breaking a long drought; excess rain later brought some mildew, but overall the impression across the state is positive. Penfolds calls it an "impressive vintage", and on release this was the wine of the year: Andrew Caillard called it "the triumph of this year's Penfolds luxury release".

**What the critics say for 2010.**
- **Andrew Caillard MW, Langton's: 100** (as listed by [Cellarit](https://www.cellarit.com.au/wine-117598-penfolds-st-henri-shiraz-2010.aspx)). "The finest vintage under this label since it was first released during the 1950s": dark chocolate, dark cherry, blackberry, mocha and roasted chestnut, then [panforte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panforte) flavours, generous sweet fruit and ripe, chocolaty tannins, finishing "graphite firm, long, and minerally".
- **[Matthew Jukes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Jukes): 20/20** and **Tony Love: 99**, as quoted by [Penfolds](https://www.penfolds.com/en-au/about-penfolds/news/penfolds-2010-st-henri-a-stand-out-from-impressive-vintage.html). Tony Love: "a multi-regional, 100% knockout SA Shiraz that excites at every step... Stunning wine that will delight for decades."
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 97+** (Lisa Perrotti-Brown, quoted by [Penfolds](https://www.penfolds.com/en-au/about-penfolds/news/penfolds-2010-st-henri-a-stand-out-from-impressive-vintage.html)). Very deep purple-black: warm blackcurrants, blueberries and licorice over mocha, cedar, menthol and grilled meat; rich, with tons of fruit structured by firm, fine tannins and refreshing acid, and great persistence. Drink 2015 to 2030-plus.
- **[James Halliday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Halliday_%28writer%29)'s Wine Companion: 97** (credited to Tyson Stelzer on [Cellarit](https://www.cellarit.com.au/wine-117598-penfolds-st-henri-shiraz-2010.aspx)). "A standout St Henri of the modern era": the gentle touch of large old vats "propels the purity and definition of a benchmark vintage"; "a shiraz of space, grace, and enduring longevity". Drink to 2040.
- **[Huon Hooke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huon_Hooke), The Real Review: 94** (March 2014). Dense and earthy, black-fruited with some raspberry, full-bodied and rich with ample tannins. "A very good St Henri." Drink 2014 to 2040.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 93.0** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is sixteen years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2020 to 2030, the Wine Advocate's runs to 2030-plus, and Halliday's Wine Companion and Hooke both say to 2040. This is exactly when St Henri starts to show what it has: the Wine Spectator vertical found the extra nuances only come with long cellaring. Expect blackcurrant and licorice turning to mocha, earth and roasted meat. Drink over the next several years; decant gently.

**Serving.** St Henri rewards patience and air. [Decant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decantation) younger bottles one to two hours ahead; older ones need only a gentle decant to leave the sediment behind. Serve at about 16 to 18°C.

**Food.** St Henri's savoury, meaty side loves roast meat. My picks: a slow-roasted leg of [lamb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamb_and_mutton) with rosemary and garlic, a [beef Wellington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beef_Wellington), [osso buco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ossobuco), roast [venison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venison), or a rich mushroom dish. Hard aged cheeses suit older bottles.

**Value and where to buy.** St Henri is easy to find on this site: ZYN in Calgary has the 2018 at $144, and the 2020 is at BC Liquor ($164.99) and BSW Liquor ($150). Older vintages turn up at auction, and the Wine Spectator piece points out St Henri sells for a fraction of Grange's price.

**From the history books**
- **A doctor's tonic.** Penfolds began making sherry- and port-style wines for Dr Penfold's patients, including a tonic for anaemia; clarets and rieslings came later ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penfolds)).
- **Mary Penfold.** After Christopher died in 1870, Mary ran the winery and blended the wines "entirely according to her judgement and taste", a journalist reported in 1874. By her retirement in 1884, Penfolds held about a third of South Australia's wine stocks ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penfolds)).
- **Grange and St Henri, born together.** Penfolds says the success of Grange "was very much enhanced by the contrasting St Henri style", and both were regarded as distinguished Australian reds within a decade of their first release ([Penfolds](https://www.penfolds.com/en-au/about-penfolds/news/penfolds-2010-st-henri-a-stand-out-from-impressive-vintage.html)).

**Curious details**
- **Auldana is gone.** The original Auldana vineyard has been "swallowed up by Adelaide housing", but St Henri remains "a reminder of Australia's old school winemaking. They had more patience in those days" ([Wine Spectator](https://www.winespectator.com/articles/penfolds-st-henri-shiraz-old-school-15540)).
- **The 1956 that never was.** Penfolds' library holds the last bottle of Davoren's first attempt, an experimental 1956 never sold. Opened for a Wine Spectator vertical, it was "still very much alive", with dried cherries, caramel and sweet earth ([Wine Spectator](https://www.winespectator.com/articles/penfolds-st-henri-shiraz-old-school-15540)).
- **Better in a half bottle.** In the same tasting, the 1962 shone brightest at 97 points, from a half bottle that was "much better" and fresher than a full-size bottle tasted first.
